VIII.57 Long's transliterated Greek kept ((aktines), (apo tou ekteinesthai)) -- RULED THE DRAFTER'S WAY AT ROUND 1 and KEPT, but the drafter's reasoning is CORRECTED as too weak: Long's English does NOT carry the etymology without the Greek. The case is as strong as VII.13's, not weaker. SETTLED in continuity.md in the corrected form.

review_round_1: review/findings-v1.md (independent reviewer session, 2026-09-12): Accept after corrections; 0 substantive, 4 minor (1.1, 7.1, 55.1, 58.1) and 4 optional preferences (1.2, 12.1, 41.1, 51.1); 54 of the 61 paragraphs 'No material issue found'. Applied in candidate-v2.json via scripts/build_book8_v2.py: all four minor findings and three of the four optional ones -- VIII.7 em dash restored to Long's comma (7.1); the four archaic 'shall' futures answered as ONE decision and removed (1.1, 55.1, 58.1), together with the reviewer's 'also noted' fourth case at VIII.51, with the resulting rule written into ../GLOSSARY.md under Voice and form; VIII.12 'peculiarly' -> 'particularly' (12.1); VIII.41 'absolutely' -> 'unconditionally' (41.1, answered by a third route: the D11 drop stands and the primary word is rendered by Long's own first alternative, rather than folding the bracket); VIII.51 'joined' reverted to Long's 'conjoined' inside the dagger clause (51.1). Declined: 1.2 only (VIII.1's quoted thought left reported rather than direct, because Long's quoted thought is in the second person while every other quoted thought in the book is in the first), recorded as considered in continuity.md. All three decisions flagged by the drafter (VIII.37 'Pergamus', VIII.57's Greek, 'effusion'/'effused') were ruled the drafter's way and are settled in continuity.md, with VIII.57's reasoning corrected to the stronger ground. The reviewer verified the step-1 no-rebuild finding three ways (re-running the build to a byte-identical file, re-reading PG lines 4933-5418 class by class, recounting the brackets) and upheld it, including the judgement that the two flush-left bracket lines in VIII.41 (PG 5247, 5249) are Long's own wrapped text and not footnote openers. All four PG slips and both PG-over-Standard-Ebooks calls (VIII.2's article, VIII.44's 'not') were located at their cited PG lines and upheld. No second round requested: no substantive finding, and every correction is confined to the clause its finding quotes.

glossary_rule_added_at_acceptance: A general voice rule was written into ../GLOSSARY.md under Voice and form at acceptance, answering findings 1.1, 55.1 and 58.1 as one decision: Long's 'shall/shalt' as a plain future (statement, or subordinate clause of condition or time) is rendered 'will' or the plain present; 'shall' is kept only where it is current English in its own right -- first person, emphatic/volitional, the deliberative 'shall' of a first- or third-person direct question, and the subjunctive of a negative consecutive clause; second-person 'shall' in a question takes 'will'. Not a rendering row; no term rendering changed. The review's premise that Books I-VI contain no second- or third-person 'shall' future is corrected in continuity.md and the ledger: three third-person plain futures stand in accepted books (III.9, VII.8, VII.24) and are listed as open, not blocking, rather than reopened.
